facts.text: Chalmette was named after plantation owner Louis‑Xavier Martin de Lino de Chalmette, a Quebec native whose family settled the area in the 1700s.
The Battle of New Orleans in January 1815 was fought on the Chalmette plantation, where Andrew Jackson’s forces defeated the British.
The Malus‑Beauregard House, a Greek Revival plantation home built in 1830, sits beside the battlefield and is open to visitors.
Since the mid‑1970s, the battlefield has been part of the Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve, with a visitor center and adjacent Chalmette National Cemetery.
In 2005 Hurricane Katrina’s storm surge flooded Chalmette, sending waters up to 15 feet high through the MRGO channel.
